title: AI Skills Beat Coding: Why Smart People Are Making the Switch Now
metaDescription: Former Google engineer says AI isn't replacing coders - just the ones who only code. Here's what actually matters now.
author: Marty @ CertFlo

sections.heading: The Skills That Matter Just Shifted
sections.body: Kelsey Hightower just said something that hit different. The former Google engineer told Business Insider that AI isn't replacing software engineers — it's replacing the ones who only know how to code. This isn't just about programmers though. The people I'm seeing do well right now all have one thing in common: they stopped trying to compete with machines and started using them instead. The ones struggling? They're still fighting a battle they can't win.

sections.heading: Why This Is Actually Good News
sections.body:
Hightower's insight shows something most people are missing: AI isn't killing jobs — it's upgrading them. But only if you see what's happening and do something about it.

The engineers who get systems and solve real problems? They're more valuable than ever. AI handles the routine stuff while they focus on architecture and strategy.

Same thing's happening everywhere else. Accountants using AI for data processing spend more time on financial strategy. Marketers who automate content creation focus on campaigns that actually work. Customer service reps who set up chatbots become customer success people.

This isn't some future thing. It's happening right now and the smart ones are already positioning themselves.

sections.heading: It's Not Really About the Tools
sections.body: Here's what separates people who get it from everyone else: they don't just use AI tools — they think about when and how to use them. They know which stuff to automate and which needs a human. They can prompt AI systems without fighting them. They spot workflow opportunities their colleagues miss completely. Most important: they've developed judgment about when AI output is good enough and when it needs work. That's not technical. That's just experience combined with common sense. The people building these skills right now are creating something close to an unfair advantage. While everyone else worries about AI taking jobs, they're using it to become irreplaceable. sections.heading: Your Move
sections.body:
Hightower's message is pretty clear: the future belongs to people who combine judgment with AI capabilities. The question isn't whether this shift is happening — it's whether you'll be ready.

The smartest people I know are already there. They didn't wait for training programs or company initiatives. They started building AI skills now, while everyone else is still debating whether it matters.
